---
title: Build a connector
description: Connect a cloud API, a desktop app, a file format or an existing MCP server.
---

<Status state="planned" />

## The recipe

<Steps>
<Step>
### Pick the type
Cloud API, desktop bridge, file, or an existing MCP server.
</Step>
<Step>
### Scaffold
`/bimai:new-connector` creates the folder and the manifest from a template.
</Step>
<Step>
### Define tools
Read tools first. Write tools always support a dry run and are safe to retry.
</Step>
<Step>
### Declare capabilities
So existing packs can use your connector.
</Step>
<Step>
### Implement and record test data
Against a real project, recorded so tests run without accounts.
</Step>
<Step>
### Certify and register
`/bimai:certify`, then `/bimai:register`, read-only first. Add a documentation page.
</Step>
</Steps>

## The contract

- Tool names: `<connector>_<resource>_<verb>`, e.g. `revit_elements_query`.
- Every result carries an evidence ID and its source.
- Errors use a shared list: `auth_expired`, `forbidden`, `not_found`, `rate_limited`, `invalid_input`,
  `app_unavailable`, `upstream_unavailable`, `conflict`.
- Secrets live in the OS keychain and never appear in results or logs.

## Desktop bridges (Revit, Civil 3D, OpenRoads, Bonsai)

- Every call runs in the app's safe context (for Revit, `ExternalEvent`).
- Every approved change is one undo step in the app.
- When the app isn't running, the connector says so clearly (`app_unavailable`).
- Declare the platforms: Revit, Civil 3D and OpenRoads bridges are Windows-only.
